title: Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.29922v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As LLMs are increasingly deployed in value-sensitive contexts, aligning them with human values has emerged as a post-training objective in NLP, aimed at instilling additional values and guiding model behaviour. However, current evaluations remain narrow. Because values are interconnected, it is unclear how fine-tuning for specific values alters unrelated capabilities and behaviours. In this work, we adapt four instruction-tuned LLMs across individual Hofstede's value dimensions and evaluate them on both cross-value transfer and broader behaviours. We find that value-specific training produces unintended side effects on untrained values, risk preferences, social cognition, and safety traits. Consequently, we suggest that value alignment after post-training should incorporate broader behavioral evaluations, and we highlight the need to investigate where additional value training might best fit into the pipeline.

translated_title: 大语言模型价值训练的意外副作用
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型越来越多地被部署在价值敏感的场景中，使其与人类价值观对齐已成为自然语言处理领域后训练阶段的一个目标，旨在向模型灌输额外的价值观并引导模型行为。然而，目前的评估仍然较为狭窄。由于各种价值观之间相互关联，针对特定价值观进行微调会如何改变模型无关的能力和行为尚不清楚。在这项工作中，作者分别在霍夫斯泰德价值理论的各个价值维度上对四个指令微调的大语言模型进行调整，并在跨价值迁移和更广泛的行为层面对其进行评估。研究发现，针对特定价值的训练会对未经训练的价值观、风险偏好、社会认知和安全特性产生意想不到的副作用。因此，作者建议在后训练之后的价值对齐过程中应纳入更广泛的行为评估，并强调需要进一步研究额外的价值训练最适合嵌入到训练流程的哪个环节。
tldr: 本文通过在霍夫斯泰德各价值维度上微调四个大语言模型，发现针对特定价值的训练会对未训练的价值观、风险偏好、社会认知和安全特性产生意外副作用，因此建议价值对齐评估应纳入更广泛的行为测试。
en_tdlr: By fine-tuning four LLMs across individual Hofstede value dimensions, this paper shows that value-specific training produces unintended side effects on untrained values, risk preferences, social cognition, and safety traits, suggesting that value alignment should incorporate broader behavioral evaluations.
